global_caption: The video consists of 10 shots and is a high-saturation anime-style steampunk mechanical city woodworking tutorial. The overall color scheme features warm copper-gold tones with cold gray metallic reflections. Lighting primarily uses practical workshop lights and backlit steam from windows. Camera movement is clear and crisp with subtle mechanical-style pushes. The entire The emotional tone remains consistently professional, focused, and encouraging.
shot1: Shot 1 opens with environment establishment using a wide overhead view with slight pan, revealing the entire woodworking workshop through dense copper pipes, rotating gears, and steam valves. In the foreground, blurred chain wheels and hanging tools pass by, while focus centers on a white female carpenter at the workbench. Composition uses depth-aligned pipes and table edges as leading lines. A warm copper-colored main light illuminates her and the wood, with faint cool-toned steam backlighting from the window. She raises her hand to indicate the wooden board and brass parts on the table, precisely mouthing “Bonjour, nous fabriquons une boîte mécanique. The camera slowly pushes in and slightly tilts down, establishing both setting and instructional subject.

The wooden board lies horizontally in the center, with metal ruler and pencil forming a clear cross composition. Shallow depth of field ensures hands and measurement lines are sharpest. Warm workshop lighting evenly covers the wood grain. fine sawdust lightly clings to the edge. A blurred brass nut appears in the foreground, while rotating gears are faintly visible in the background, creating layered depth of the mechanical workshop. Warm key light from the upper left highlights the board’s edge and fingertips. She slides the board into the fixed clamp and adds a marking with a pencil at the cutting position. Wood grain and lead marks are clearly visible. The camera performs a short push-in, drawing viewer attention to the marked point and clamp tension.

Background keeps soft-focus copper pipes and pressure gauges. Lighting remains warm copper-based, with cool flashes on saw teeth. She steadily pulls the saw to cut the side panel, shoulder and arm movements fluid. The board edge gradually separates. Her sleeve and apron edges sway slightly with motion. Foreground shows palm edge, background scattered fine sawdust on the table. Workshop warm light emphasizes dust texture. She sands back and forth evenly, rough edges gradually becoming smooth and rounded. Material transformation is clearly visible in a short time. As “Lissez bien.
shot6: Shot 6 cuts hard to a near-eye-level slightly overhead close-up. Centered are the pre-trimmed side panel corners and a small hand drill. Foreground and background framed by workbench edge and blurred gears. Lighting continues warm workshop illumination with clear highlight on the drill bit. She first marks positions with a pointed tool, then steadily pre-drills four corner holes. Fine wood shavings circle and regular holes appear on the surface. The French “Percez aux coins. ” synchronizes with each downward press. The camera makes a slight forward push then stops, emphasizing hole alignment accuracy.
shot7: Shot 7 cuts hard to an overhead medium-close shot. Several cut panels and a pair of brass hinges are neatly arranged on the table. Composition resembles an assembly diagram, with panel edges forming parallel leading lines. Focus evenly covers the test-fit area. Warm light makes wood appear solid, brass components gleam subtly at edges. She sequentially test-fits side, bottom, and front panels, then places brass hinges near the lid to compare fit. Gaps, angles, and edge alignment are clearly visible. The camera slowly pans horizontally, sweeping across all connection points.
shot8: Shot 8 cuts hard to an eye-level medium shot. The workbench is slightly pulled back to show full coordination of hands, clamps, glue, and screwdriver. Foreground shows open glue bottle, background still features operating steam equipment. Lighting maintains consistent warm tone with translucent reflection on glue edges. She applies glue along seams, quickly closes the panels, then uses a small screwdriver to tighten connections. The wooden box transitions from loose parts to a stable 3D structure. The French “Assemblez maintenant. ” precisely aligns with her pressing the box into shape and tightening the final turn. The camera first gently pushes in, then slightly orbits to the side-front, showing structural closure while maintaining step clarity.
shot9: Shot 9 cuts hard into a pushing close-up eye-level shot. Focus is on the lid edge, brass hinge, and gear-shaped handle. Composition uses a diagonal third-rule placement of the box. Foreground shows her hand holding the lid, background blurs into mechanical silhouettes of the cityscape emitting steam from the window. Warm key light illuminates brass textures, backlight outlines the lid. She aligns the hinge with pre-drilled holes, then screws on the gear handle. Lid opens and closes smoothly, with the gear handle flashing highlights during rotation. The French “Ajoutez la charnière. ” corresponds sequentially to hinge attachment, screw insertion, and handle tightening. The camera continuously pushes in and slightly lifts, highlighting the refined detail after mechanical decoration completion.
shot10: The 10th shot transitions from the previous shot with a slight fade-in/fade-out to a medium close-up at eye level, ending with the finished product storage box placed centrally on the workbench. The composition centers the box as the main subject, with several neatly arranged excess brass parts in the foreground and the steam-punk mechanical city's rising white mist and rotating tower wheels visible through the workshop's high windows in the background. The depth of field is moderate, keeping the finished product sharp while giving the city silhouette an atmospheric quality. Warm copper lighting wraps around the wooden box surface, highlighting its clean edges and polished gear handle. She lifts the box with both hands, gently opens and closes the lid, demonstrating smooth hinge operation and overall capacity, then smiles with satisfaction. The French phrase 'C’est fini, bravo!' synchronizes with the final product freeze-frame, while the ambient steam hiss subtly rises at the end of the sentence and naturally fades out. The camera performs one last steady push-in, stopping on the intricate details of the lid and handle, forming a complete, clear, and visually compelling steam-punk tutorial conclusion.
